To be honest, what doomed WW2 shooters was how samey they were. And I honestly think that that's a result of developers not realising that it basically covered the whole damn world.

There were engagements on the land, sea and sky on pretty much every corner of the planets surface with enough people and material to feild a reasonable force. You had strategic bombing campaigns going on in Western Europe while the east saw horrifically bloody combined arms warfare, with high level armour engements occurring all over North Africa while Burma and India saw absolutely hellish jungle warfare and Asia was seeing one of the largest single naval offensives in modern history. The war started with prop aircraft and conventional bombing being the newest tactics and ended with rocketry going serious, the first jet aircraft coming off the drawing board, and America harnessing the Atom to produce weapons so powerful they arguably went on to make war obsolete. The first instances of what would go on to define the modern world stood cheek by jowl with the last remnants of the old order making on last attempt to get in the history books or die trying. Basically, understanding the modern world requires you to accept it as a partial consequence of a war which radically changed the established social, political and international order.

And yet all the shooters focused on was the same bits of European countryside over and over again.

I'm sure a lot of people would like to see them look around the whole conflict a bit more. I'd like to put in the shoes of the Red Army as they go from a panicked swarm on the defensive to one of the most enduring combined arms powers of the war. I want to see the British fighting in Burma against the enemy, their own limited resources, and the very nature of the jungle that served as the battlefield. I want to be put in the shoes of some Yankee infantry grunt trying to survive the horrifically dangerous island warfare of the Pacific campaigns, while dealing with an enemy with motivations more comparable to a suicide cult than any sane military power. And with our modern capabilities, we can make that all pop right out of our screens like we're almost there ourselves.

It's more than time we thought about giving the WW2 shooter the treatment it deserves.
